name: Virtue USD
oneLiner: VUSD is Virtue Money's CDP dollar on IOTA, minted by borrowing against overcollateralized IOTA and stIOTA positions with liquidation defending the peg.
collateral: Overcollateralized IOTA, stIOTA, and IBTC (bridged BTC) positions backing VUSD debt inside the Virtue Money protocol
pegMechanism: CDP-style mint: users borrow VUSD against IOTA or stIOTA collateral and repay debt to unlock collateral, with liquidation and redemption mechanics supporting the U.S. dollar peg

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Virtue is a crypto-collateralized protocol, but the IOTA deployment is not yet represented in Pharos contract metadata and available sources do not prove the absence of admin or pause surfaces.

mintAuthority.summary: VUSD is on IOTA Rebased (Move VM). The package at 0xd3b63e...904f is immutable, but contains an admin module. An AdminCap object (0x38a7b38d...) is held by EOA/address 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12. AdminCap gates set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, and set_beneficiary — active admin privileges over mint supply.

controls.label: Virtue Money borrower-operations / branch contracts (Liquity V2 fork)
controls.capDescription: Mint bounded by overcollateralized CDPs across IOTA/stIOTA branches with user-set interest rates, per the Liquity V2 multi-collateral design.
controls.evidence: Virtue docs describe VUSD as minted by opening overcollateralized CDPs using IOTA/stIOTA on a Liquity V2 friendly fork on IOTA EVM with user-set rates, flash minting, and liquidation/redemption peg defense.

controls.label: Virtue Money AdminCap holder
controls.evidence: At IOTA Rebased (confirmed via iota_getObject): AdminCap object 0x38a7b38d0f03338397d1c57f2cc2e3d7c5e3f6fe6887626aacc4cb4e8072c3f5 is owned by AddressOwner 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (version 591278735). Package 0xd3b63e...904f is Immutable (no upgrade). The admin module exposes no public entry functions but AdminCap gates vusd::set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, and set_beneficiary. Whether this address is a single EOA or a multisig could not be determined on-chain.

review.evidence: IOTA Rebased GraphQL confirmed AdminCap (type 0xd3b63e...::admin::AdminCap) is held by address 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (AddressOwner). iota_getNormalizedMoveModulesByPackage revealed vusd module exposing set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, set_beneficiary — all AdminCap-gated. Package owner type = Immutable (cannot be re-published). The AdminCap holder address owns no other enumerable objects, so it may be a multisig or single-keypair; cannot confirm threshold/type from chain state alone. Promotion judgment: the AdminCap holder address is confirmed on-chain; on Move-VM chains an address holder is EOA-equivalent (single-key vs k-of-n keypair custody is indistinguishable from chain state, matching the EVM EOA custody rule and the standard applied to BUCK and suiUSDe on Sui). All mint-capable surfaces (immutable branch contracts; parameter-only AdminCap) are confirmed.
